inputs.text: Standing at the mouth of a mural alley beside a corner store in a Bay Area neighborhood at blue hour. On the corner a small bodega with a lit awning, hand-painted signage and a neon OPEN sign; along the alley a long brick wall with a half-finished mural and layers of old tags, dumpsters, a fire escape, a chain-link fence, an empty curbside spot under a string of bulbs, wet asphalt reflecting sodium-orange streetlights against a deep blue sky, light fog. Photorealistic, physically plausible light, wistful melancholy-beautiful West Coast dusk. No people, no cars.
